newsitem.title: GERMANY: Firm dollar drives German DAX to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Firm dollar drives German DAX to new highs.

text.p: The seemingly unstoppable German share market soared further on Monday, as the strong dollar propelled the blue chip DAX past yet another psychologically crucial level -- 4,100 points.
Export shares and heavyweight insurance stocks led an advance that sent the DAX powering up 83.22 points, or 2.06 percent, to a record high close of 4,124.19 points.
Although volumes were relatively modest, the mood was upbeat, dealers said.
"This doesn't surprise me in the least," said one Frankfurt trader. "It's totally justified at this dollar level. There is not a single weak signal out there."

The dollar was hovering at a six-year high of around 1.79 marks thoughout the share trading session, providing further grounds for optimism for Germany's largely export-driven chemical, car and engineering sectors.
Chemical companies Hoechst, Bayer and BASF were trading heavily and firmly keeping up with overall market gains.
Hoechst was up 1.45 marks at 80 marks, Bayer up 1.40 at 73.85 and BASF up 58 pfennigs at 67.55 marks.
Electronics and engineering giant Siemens, continuing a spate of popularity, was up 2.05 marks at 114.65.
Insurance shares were surging, boosted by a better than expected earnings report on Friday from reinsurer Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG.
Munich Re, whose earnings per share rose to a record 150 marks for 1996/1997, advanced 400 marks, or nearly seven percent, to 6,325 marks.
Allianz AG, which owns 25 percent of Munich Re, was up 17 marks, or 4.1 percent, at 433 marks.
